reason: The reclaimed reflector looks suited to completing the shadeless bench lamp.
expectation: The reflector will fit onto the lamp, preparing it to light the repair bench.

effect: The reflector fitted the lamp, leaving it ready to connect to power.
reaction: The existing collar made that a satisfying straightforward repair.
reason: The shielded low-voltage lamp needs power to provide steady bench light.
expectation: The power supply will light the bench lamp.

effect: The powered lamp completed the bench-light goal; the market lighting remains.
reaction: The warm light is a pleasing payoff for the repair.
reason: The detached fused lead appears to belong on the charged market battery before it can power the lights.
expectation: The fused lead will connect to the market battery.

effect: The battery and fused lead now form a protected supply for the market lights.
reaction: The bounded supply makes the repair feel practical.
reason: The disconnected market light strips need the portable supply to illuminate the market.
expectation: The supply will power the market light strips.

effect: The strips needed their connectors repaired before being powered; they are now reconnected but uncovered.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the missing repair step.
reason: The translucent sign offcuts may cover the exposed light strips before they are powered.
expectation: The offcuts will cover the strips and diffuse their light.

alternatives.reason: The repaired strips may be ready for power, but their uncovered state suggests adding the offcuts first.

effect: The offcuts covered the strips and protected their connectors; the market lights still need power.
reaction: The offcuts serve a satisfying practical purpose as both covers and diffusers.
reason: The covered market lights are unpowered, and the protected portable supply is ready.
expectation: The supply will power the covered market lights.

effect: The market lights are working on local power; marking what the map omits remains.
reaction: The illuminated stalls make the missing-map problem feel concrete.
reason: Moth's cached service map and the lit market may combine to mark the place the map leaves out.
expectation: The lit market will provide evidence to mark the missing area on Moth's map.

effect: Marking the lit stalls on Moth's map completed the market goal and made the distinction between a directory gap and an empty place explicit.
reaction: The map update was a satisfying way to connect the repair to the neighborhood's larger problem.

mostWorthwhile.text: Powering the market lights and marking the stalls on the map made the physical repair matter to the story as well as the people using the market.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the reflector and then the power supply was straightforward and predictable, though it established the repair clearly.

surprise.text: I expected to power the disconnected strips immediately, but they first needed their connectors repaired; the compatibility feedback performed that repair automatically.

arbitrary.text: Marking the map by combining it with the powered lights was a little abstract, though the result explained that June marked the visible stalls on the export.

continue.text: Yes. The contrast between the functioning neighborhood and its absence from the directory makes me curious how the broader problem will unfold, and the practical repairs were satisfying.
